## Where this goes

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="44%"}
- `ConvolvedDistributions.jl` adds sums and differences of delays
- The generation time is the same shape of problem, a convolution and
  a difference
- A composed Julia `epidist`, with Turing submodels doing what the
  `brms` formula does now

::: {.callout-important}
The `epidist` layer on top is not written yet. Open issue
`CensoredDistributions.jl#749` says the joint fit is too slow.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
![](../figures/fig-si-compose.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A graph of a composed delay. A latent period and a
transmission delay combine into a generation time, the generation time
and a difference of incubation periods combine into a serial interval,
and double interval censoring turns that into the observed delay."}

```julia
using CensoredDistributions
using ConvolvedDistributions, Distributions

incubation = Gamma(2.0, 1.0)
reporting = LogNormal(1.0, 0.5)

d = convolved(incubation, reporting)
observed = double_interval_censored(
    d; upper = 15, interval = 1
)

cdf(observed, 5.0)   # 0.4561
```

::: {.attribution}
Diagram from
[How to serial interval?](https://samabbott.co.uk/how-to-serial-interval),
labelled there for a serial interval ·
Plain `Distributions.jl` dispatch, composed for this talk rather than
lifted from a README. Run against `CensoredDistributions.jl` v0.2.22
and
[ConvolvedDistributions.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/ConvolvedDistributions.jl).
Neither package appears in the other's `[deps]`, and both list
`Distributions`
